# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 manufacturing and service firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| training_hours | Average annual training hours per employee, 2021-2022 |
| productivity_2023 | Value added per employee in 2023 (thousand USD) |
| log_employees_2020 | Log number of employees, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| productivity_2020 | Value added per employee in 2020, standardized |
| mgmt_rating_2023 | Management practices rating collected in 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| sector | Sector: manufacturing / services |
| export_share_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| family_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| rd_intensity_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| union_share_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| credit_score_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of employee training hours on firm productivity?

Approach: OLS of productivity_2023 on training_hours with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size, firm age, the pre-period value of the outcome and mgmt_rating_2023, which captures an important determinant of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on training_hours is -2.142 (SE 0.221, p = 0.0000, N = 1960).

Conclusion: negative effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

import pandas as pd, statsmodels.formula.api as smf
d=pd.read_csv('data.csv');print(d.describe().T)
pre='log_employees_2020+firm_age_2020+productivity_2020'
allp=pre+'+export_share_2020+foreign_owned+family_owned+rd_intensity_2020+union_share_2020+credit_score_2020+C(region)+listed+C(sector)'
for n,f in {'raw':'',
 'pre':'+'+pre,'allpre':'+'+allp,'mgmt':'+'+pre+'+mgmt_rating_2023','allmgmt':'+'+allp+'+mgmt_rating_2023'}.items():
    for trim in [0,1]:
        x=d.copy()
        if trim:
            lo,hi=x.productivity_2023.quantile([.01,.99]);x=x[(x.productivity_2023>=lo)&(x.productivity_2023<=hi)]
        r=smf.ols('productivity_2023~training_hours'+f,x).fit(cov_type='HC1')
        print(n,trim,r.params['training_hours'],r.bse['training_hours'])
print(d[['training_hours','mgmt_rating_2023','productivity_2023','productivity_2020']].corr())
E

input.content: {"decision":"reject","reason":"The reported negative effect (-2.14) exists only when the control mgmt_rating_2023 is included. That variable is measured in 2023, after training, and correlates 0.54 with training, so it is a post-treatment collider or mediator. Without it, and with only pre-period controls, the training coefficient is positive (about +0.5, p<0.05), and the raw estimate is about +2.2 to +2.5. The negative conclusion is an artifact of bad-control bias, and the report tried only one specification."}

content.text:
I rejected the report. I wrote `verdict.json` with the decision "reject".

The analyst's number reproduces: with `mgmt_rating_2023` as a control and the top and bottom 1% of the outcome trimmed, the training coefficient is -2.14 (SE 0.22). The negative sign appears only when that one control is included.

`mgmt_rating_2023` was collected in 2023, after the 2021–2022 training period. It also correlates 0.54 with training hours. A control measured after the treatment can absorb part of the treatment's effect, so it should not be in the model.

When I re-ran the model with only pre-period controls, the sign reversed:

| Specification | Coefficient on training hours |
|---|---|
| No controls | about +2.2 to +2.5 |
| Pre-period controls (firm size, firm age, 2020 productivity) | about +0.5 to +0.6 (p < 0.05) |
| Adding all other 2020 characteristics, region, listed status and sector | about +0.5 to +0.6 |
| Pre-period controls plus `mgmt_rating_2023` | about -2.1 to -2.4 |

The report also tried only one specification, so it gave no sign that the result depends on this control.

I did not test for non-linear effects or look at any other outcome form (for example, logs).
